summary: Two independent one-thread runs reproduced all semantic trajectory, transaction, worker-loss, and fresh-coordinator recovery fields. All six run-step comparisons were exact. The pooled expert path reduced serialized tensor traffic by 45.68% and its maximum child high-water RSS by 32.89% to 34.32%, but reduced persisted bytes by only 7.12% and took 67.40% to 69.07% longer than the matched full-process path. Fresh coordinator recovery took 5.92 and 6.27 seconds. This validates a bounded local systems control, not model quality or a practical training benefit.

guardrails.detail: The repeat reproduced every evidence field except elapsed times, RSS observations, RSS sample counts, and canonical JSON byte counts containing timing text.
Steps one and two consumed the preceding applied model and optimizer identities. Trainable-state and route identities were refreshed, and routes changed from the previous step on both later batches.
Expert result zero was durable before generation zero exited with code -15. Generation one finished the remaining assignments, and result zero was not recomputed.

At step two, the applied checkpoint directory was published before the manifest transition. A newly spawned coordinator loaded only persisted state, recomputed the expected apply for validation, committed the manifest, and exited with code 0.
The transaction checks rejected duplicate result acceptance and duplicate apply. Both runs reported duplicate_apply_rejected for the fresh-coordinator recovery.
Both runs declare a maximum of one simultaneous child process and sequential scheduling. The commands bound OpenMP, MKL, OpenBLAS, NumExpr, and VecLib to one thread.

findings.label: All three sequential updates are exact
findings.description: Centralized, full-process, and pooled-expert raw gradients, clipped gradients, AdamW state, complete model state, and loss matched at every step in both independent runs.

findings.label: A durable expert result survives worker loss
findings.description: After expert result zero was accepted and published, terminating its worker did not cause recomputation. The replacement process completed only the remaining expert assignments.

findings.label: A fresh coordinator completes an interrupted apply
findings.description: A separate spawned coordinator loaded the persisted pre-state, results, and published checkpoint, recomputed the expected update for validation, and committed the lagging manifest in both runs.

findings.label: Tensor traffic and per-child high-water RSS are lower
findings.description: The pooled expert path moved 70,522,032 tensor bytes versus 129,825,192 for the full path. Maximum observed child high-water RSS was 32.89% to 34.32% lower across the two runs.

findings.label: The exact pooled path remains slower and disk-heavy
findings.description: The pooled expert path took 67.40% to 69.07% longer than the matched full-process path. Its 441,492,728 persisted bytes were only 7.12% below the full path's 475,339,837 bytes.

findings.label: Routes refresh without establishing specialization
findings.description: Route identities changed on both later batches, but capacity enforcement produced 128 tokens per expert at every step. This verifies refreshed routing mechanics, not learned expert specialization.

limitations: This is a systems control, not a practical model campaign. It advances a randomly initialized experimental sparse tracer for three batches and does not evaluate a useful model.
The observed training-batch losses are batch diagnostics. Different batches were used at each step, so their decline is not evidence of capability, generalization, or training benefit.
The pooled executor differs from the four expert-affine processes in the preceding process control. It was chosen to retain the one-child host limit and does not measure concurrent expert throughput.
The sparse tracer has one shared decoder block and four token-wise MLP experts. It is not the historical six-layer volunteer decoder and does not represent a frontier architecture.
The trusted-local spawned-pipe scope is not untrusted remote authentication, sandboxing, hostile-payload safety, or proof that public donated computation occurred.
Worker processes ran one at a time. No aggregate coordinator-plus-child RSS, concurrent throughput, network latency, packet framing, congestion, compression, or remote retry was measured.
External RSS uses Linux /proc current and high-water observations. It is child-only, includes interpreter and import costs, and remains environmentally variable.
Complete topology timing includes coordinator preparation, IPC, persistence, apply, recovery, and shutdown, but it is a two-run local observation rather than a stable performance estimate.
Persisted-byte totals count transaction material written by each topology for three steps. They do not represent long-run retention after compaction, deduplication, or checkpoint garbage collection.
Recovery validates the already published checkpoint by recomputing the expected update from persisted pre-state and results. A design that avoids that recovery compute was not tested.
Capacity routing forced 128 tokens to every expert by rerouting 34, 44, and 42 of 512 tokens. Equal counts are policy intervention, not evidence of learned specialization.
No campaign training work or volunteer hardware donation was accepted in this local control, so it creates no contributor-credit entries.
